findings.rationale: This signal is asserted when the counter reaches a specific terminal count value. In isolation it appears as a normal counter feature, but it is routed to the top module where it is combined with other signals to form a rare-event trigger condition. Its presence as a dedicated output suggests it may serve as a trigger fragment for a hardware Trojan.

This signal is asserted when a specific command is decoded. While command matching is a standard function, this signal is exported to the top module and combined with other signals. The specific command value may be chosen to create a rare trigger condition, making it a likely trigger fragment.

This signal latches high on any error and remains asserted until reset. It is a sticky error flag that, when combined with other signals at the top level, can contribute to a trigger condition. Its sticky nature ensures the trigger can be activated by a transient error, making it a plausible trigger fragment.

A multiplexer or conditional assignment in the top module selects the least significant bit of secret_reg (secret_reg[0]) and drives it onto the status_out port when the combined trigger signal (AND of counter_terminal, command_match, and sticky_error) is active. This leaks internal secret data to an external observer, constituting the payload of a hardware Trojan.
